utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Do you hear me, Mr. Seselj? Good afternoon, Mr. Seselj. Do you follow the proceedings in the language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As usual, I can follow the proceedings only in the Serbian language. Right now, I am receiving interpretation into Serbian, so I can follow the proceedings. But it is important for me to point out, invariably, that it's the Serbian language, because I do not allow The Hague Tribunal to change the name of my mother tongue and call it "Croatian," and "Bosnian" as well, and who knows what else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My understanding is that we are in the middle of hearing the cross-examination of Mr. Drazilovic. Let's bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Drazilovic. Was it Mr. MacFarlane or Ms. Wanlin to continue? Yes, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe that when we left off in cross-examination yesterday afternoon, that we were in private session, and then we moved briefly into public for procedural matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll go back to private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in private session. Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday in your evidence, if I recall correctly, and you can correct me if I'm wrong, you had indicated that at a very, very early stage, before you had any contact with the Office of the Prosecutor, that you had a discussion with Mr. Seselj. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: And that he had suggested that you go to the Office of the Prosecutor and --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, there is no reason for this to be in closed session, absolutely no reason whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just bear with it for the moment. We'll see whether we can lift the confidentiality or not. I can't find it at this moment. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: We'll be moving into it within one or two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Sir, you also indicated, if I recall correctly, that Mr. Seselj had suggested that you speak to the OTP and that you be truthful. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Do you recall meeting with one or more of the investigators around the 13th of September, 2003, at the Tribunal's Belgrade office, and that it was a circumstance in which you had requested the meeting to discuss various issues?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I could refresh your memory a bit more. The meeting was requested by you to discuss protective measures, in view of the disclosure of a statement and possible testimony before the Tribunal. Does that assist you at all?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it didn't assist me at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I could attempt to refresh your memory further by referring to some more specific details and see if that jogs your memory. Do you recall advising the investigators that while on vacation on the coast in Montenegro, you felt that someone was chasing you? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, some references are called for here. On the basis of what is Mr. MacFarlane putting these questions? This is not contained in the preliminary witness statements at all. We do have to have some sort of reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, I would like you -- I would like to request to you not to interfere with the cross-examination. If necessary, I take it that Mr. MacFarlane is ready to give reference later on, but don't interrupt with the flow of his cross-examination. Let's proceed, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: With a view to perhaps jogging your memory, do you recall advising the investigators that a few days after an interview with the Office of the Prosecutor, you visited the Serbian Radical Party offices to check on the situation to see how things were going, and you were wanting to see the reaction of the members of the party in respect of a statement that you had provided to the OTP? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall this either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Do you recall advising the investigators that you met strange people around your building and in the street and on the buses, and that that had happened seven or eight times from the date that you had given the statement to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I may remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Is the meeting coming back to you a bit more now, and the discussions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember this meeting, but I did have the impression -- now, was it due to some fear or something else? I had the impression that I was being followed by someone. It is quite possible, and I said that to my family members, and my son said, Daddy, maybe this is paranoia or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Do you recall advising the investigators that you thought you might be coming -- be becoming a bit obsessed and slightly paranoid because of the things that you were seeing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I said that my son said that to me, that he noticed this form of paranoia, it is possible, but I really do not remember this conversation with the investigators on that date that you referred to. I think that I had a contact with them before Dr. Vojislav Seselj voluntarily surrendered to The Hague. I really do not recall this date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Do you recall another meeting, perhaps with another date, that involved the discussions that I've just outlined to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I think it was only then that I was on the premises of The Hague Tribunal in Belgrade, sometime before Dr. Seselj went to The Hague voluntarily. As for these previous dates that you've referred to, I really do not remember any of that, and I don't even know whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Do you recall having a discussion with the investigators around the period of time that I've just mentioned, where you discussed protective measures and requested that your statement, if it's to be used in legal proceedings, be used with a pseudonym and delayed disclosure?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, during this first contact with the people from the OTP, I said that whenever my name is mentioned, let it be in public, without any protective measures whatsoever. I didn't ask for any protection. There was no need for me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: You have some recollection of some things and many non-recollections. Is this perhaps attributable to the confusion and forgetfulness that you referred to yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, that's the reason. I tell you, I remember that first meeting with the people from The Hague Tribunal, that it was sometime just before Dr. Vojislav Seselj went to The Hague voluntarily. I do not remember that date that you mentioned a moment ago. What was it that you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: So some of the things --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. MacFarlane, do we need to remain in private session? If you could remind me of the reason why we should be in private session for this topic, if necessary in the absence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I will be tendering a document in the next while, and I believe that it ought to be tendered in private session. I'm moving into another area. The witness doesn't recall the matters that I've raised, and so I've gone as far as I can on that issue. I will move to another one that does involve a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to move to another area. Yesterday, you indicated, if I recall correctly, that at one point you were appointed to the position of the head of War Staff for the Serbian Radical Party. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After Ljubisa Petkovic resigned, I was appointed chief of the War Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: And I take it that would be a position of considerable authority. It was a position that required a good person and who could handle a lot of situations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my job as chief of the War Staff was a normal thing, a usual thing. Our job there, the job of the team there, was to take in refugees, and then later on, when I became chief of the War Staff, it had to do with the organisation and sending of volunteers to threatened territories. In principle, that was it. Nothing special happened, except if we perhaps collected food and cigarettes, in particular, for the people we were sending out into the field. That was it, and later on, going to see the wounded in hospitals, and also the families of these wounded persons. And, unfortunately, it was also my job to receive the families of volunteers who had lost their lives and to help them with procedural matters. That is to say, it had to do with the Military Hospital, knowing people there, preparations regarding the transportation of the deceased to their places of burial. It had to do with that, primarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, you referred, in direct examination, to a meeting that you had with a Prosecutor. I believe you indicated it was Ms. Dahl, and I believe you indicated that it was -- you thought it was around 2007. Is that recollection of mine --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, all of that was in public session yesterday. We are still in private session. We haven't seen a single reason for being in private session until now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I propose to tender a document at this point. I was endeavouring to lay the foundation for the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: The meeting that you had with Ms. Dahl and others, I suggest, took place around the 16th of November, 2007. Would that sound about right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, it's quite possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Did you have more than one meeting with Ms. Dahl or just simply one?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to show you a document. It is both in English and in Serbian and contains signatures. I would like you to take a look at it. It purports to be a transcript of a meeting, and my question is whether or not this is a transcript of the meeting to which you made reference.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I read this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So the question was whether this was a transcript of the meeting the witness had referred to. Mr. Drazilovic, can you help us, whether this is a transcript of the meeting you referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Yesterday, when you testified with respect to this meeting, you were proceeding on the basis of your memory, and you indicated that you were forgetful. So would you agree that this is the best evidence of what took place?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want to ask you to comment on a few things. There was a lawyer with you at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was required at this meeting to come over here and to testify as a witness for the Prosecution. I refused that straight away, because in my earliest statements, I had said that I can go to The Hague solely as a witness for the defence of Dr. Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, that wasn't my question. My question was to you: I understand that a lawyer was with you at the time of this meeting.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: And I understand further that that lawyer or that person was part of the Seselj Defence team. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: So you were relying on the resources of the Seselj Defence team in order to meet with the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Ms. Dahl advised you that you can expect to receive a summons, and then further asked you if you would respond to the summons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she asked me that, but I said I would only come as a witness for the defence of Dr. Vojislav Seselj, and I persistently repeated that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Ms. Dahl then discussed arrangements that could be made for you, in terms of Victims Services, being picked up, allowing you to look at documents to refresh your memory, and so on. She was outlining the process, the procedure involved in testifying; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what is etched in my memory, and after reading this document, she, in fact, requested me to come here as a witness for the Prosecution, and she offered some privileges to me. She asked me if I wanted something, how much I wanted, do I need some clothes, do I need an escort, so all kinds of benefits. However, in response, I said, yes, I would come as a witness to The Hague, but only as a witness for the defence of Dr. Vojislav Seselj, and I didn't back off on this, so in terms of all these offers that she made. And you can see in the minutes of the meeting I said eventually that I'm not prepared to discuss this matter any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: She was outlining the support that's provided to witnesses who testify at the Tribunal, wasn't she?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in principle, but it seems as if she was making all kinds of offers just to persuade me to come over here as a witness for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Near the end of the meeting, Ms. Dahl asked you about your first contact with the Defence team. Initially, you said: "I don't know the exact date, but it was a long time ago." She asked further questions on that, and you said: "I said what I said. I have said what I have to say."

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: You were unwilling to answer that question?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't prepared at the time to answer these kind of questions that she put to me. I mentioned in my earlier statements that I was maintaining a constant contact with members of the Serbian Radical Party. Being a member, I used to go to the party headquarters, I visited all the rallies or professional and scientific panels and discussions that were organised with a view to providing defence for Dr. Vojislav Seselj. So I always said, If you need something, please call me. Therefore, I asked Ms. Dahl and this previous man - what was his name? - Paolo, if they wanted to call me again, they should do that through my lawyer. Any personal call that came from them at a later stage caused stress and fear in me, quite substantial fear, because having realised what the crux and the essence of the questions were that I was being asked, I realised what it was. I'm sorry, I just lost the plot a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: One of the questions that Ms. Dahl asked you near the end of the meeting was this: "Has anyone told you not to testify against Mr. Seselj?" And your response was: "I said that I would only testify for Mr. Seselj's defence. I said this at the beginning." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. But as I understood it, that was in the context of whether I was threatened by anyone from the Serbian Radical Party. I was persistently and constantly in contact with Dr. Vojislav Seselj's Defence team and other people from the party. I used to go there. We saw each other on a regular basis. So I just couldn't understand why she was asking this question in this way, because it seems that she was suggesting that I should say that I was afraid from someone; for example, Ljubisa Petkovic. As you can see from my answer, you can see that I was adamant and I refused to discuss this matter any further, because I thought that what I said before was quite enough, as far as that meeting went.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, Mr. MacFarlane. Speaking for myself, I'm struggling to see how this line of questioning is relevant to this case. So you're minded to tender this transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Yes. I intend to draw my questions to a close within the next minute or so, and I endeavour to demonstrate the relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the reason why we should stay in private session was that this document is a confidential document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I would like you to conclude as soon as possible on this topic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: The question that Ms. Dahl posed to you: "Has anyone told you not to testify against Mr. Seselj," with the greatest of respect, you haven't answered that question. I would like to ask you that question again, and I would appreciate a direct answer. Has anyone told you not to testify against Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody ever, anywhere, told me to testify against Dr. Vojislav Seselj, and I am particularly referring to the people from the Serbian Radical Party. Never, never. There was no need for that. I was with the people from the Serbian Radical Party virtually on a daily basis. We used to meet, we socialised, we went fishing, and other pastimes, so I would also meet with them whenever I needed help, and they were always considerate enough to oblige. So nobody ever, from the Serbian Radical Party, threatened me or tried to force me to come here and be a witness for the Prosecution, because that's really -- I'm still --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Sir, I have one final question for you, and it's this: You've indicated that you were the head of War Staff and had a very responsible and difficult position, and yet you've indicated that you were intimidated and there is a rough attitude during the course of this interview. You're a very experienced person, you've had rough times before. How could you possibly have been intimidated during the course of this interview as recorded in this statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before Mr. Drazilovic answers that question, I wonder whether we cannot go back to open session for this answer, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And if you could repeat your question again in public session. We'll go back to open session, Mr. Drazilovic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: If it could help, I could back up a few questions to provide context so that there is context in the public portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, please do so, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: During the course of a discussion with the Prosecution in November of 2007, you met with Ms. Christine Dahl, who is a Prosecutor with the Tribunal, and she posed this question to you: "Has anyone told you not to testify against Mr. Seselj?" And your response was: "I said that I would only testify for Mr. Seselj's defence. I said this at the beginning." My suggestion to you, sir, is that you did not really answer the question that was posed. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not exactly. I believe that my response contained the answer to her question, and I immediately added that I only want to testify as a witness for the defence of Dr. Vojislav Seselj. But it seems that something remained unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: During the course of your testimony, you have indicated that you were the head of the War Staff for the Serbian Radical Party, it was a difficult position, it was a position of responsibility, and you dealt with difficult issues all the time. We have evidence of what actually occurred at this meeting, and you indicated that you felt it was an intimidation, you felt that it was a rough meeting. I would like you to explain how it's possible that you felt intimidated, given the fact that -- given the reality of what we now know took place during that interview. We have a transcript.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is possible, to put it simply. Why shouldn't it be, because they took such an approach? So I'm going back again to my first encounter with the investigator called Paolo, and his arrogance and his threats that I would go to jail, that I would be fined, that if I failed to confirm something that he knew, and he asked me to confirm certain things, and I disagreed. And something started happening with me. I was becoming depressed, I was losing my nerves, and I had to be treated medically. So it is only natural for a person to snap under such circumstances, regardless of the fact that I did this job as the chief of the Crisis Staff. I obviously had skills for performing this duty. But as I said, this was not any kind of special job. Anyone could have done it. It just happened that I was chosen to do it. However, when it comes to these interrogations that I was subjected to by the Tribunal's investigators, it had a tremendous psychological impact on me, especially when she started offering me certain benefits, remunerations, or some luxurious circumstances that I would be given access to if I decided to come here. They said they would be taking me out for dinner and things like that. So as a result, I suffered a breakdown, literally speaking, and I felt very bad, psychologically. So my status had nothing to do with the job that I was performing, because anyone could have done it. Of course, there were some painful moments, especially during funerals and meetings with the bereaved families, but that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for your perspective on the interview. Of course, the transcript will ultimately speak for itself, in terms of what was said during the course of the meeting. I'd like to move to the final area, which won't be lengthy. You indicated during direct examination with Mr. Seselj that your position is that you will not testify on behalf of the Prosecution and you will not testify on behalf of the Chamber; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always maintained that I want to testify as a witness for the defence of Dr. Vojislav Seselj. That's what I have always been saying. Why would I appear as a witness in a different context? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Is it fair, then, to say that you are a supporter of Mr. Seselj and, in essence, have become a part of his team?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I absolutely am a supporter of Dr. Vojislav Seselj. I have known him for a long time. I don't know why I would testify against him. I thought that I was summoned here, but nobody ever asked me a question which comes out necessarily, why I would come here, because my name appeared in some of his books. But weren't those books published after the protective measures had been lifted, as far as I was concerned? Therefore, I don't see any reason for me to testify against Dr. Vojislav Seselj. I am honoured to be mentioned in his books.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: My point, sir, is that you are a supporter of Mr. Seselj, and I suggest to you that you don't want to see anything bad happen to him in this trial. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes, that's correct. There are certain charges brought here that are absolutely baseless and have nothing to do with the events that took place. And I'm not the only one who thinks this. The majority of the Serbian people share this opinion. Mr. Seselj is not defending himself so much as he's defending the Serbian people and everything that has been happening with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: In relation to the specific charge before this Chamber, namely, one of contempt of the Tribunal, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. MacFarlane. You tendered that transcript into evidence? That's already in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: We have not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He forgot to tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: It was not formally tendered. I would seek to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have any objection, Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I have only two short supplementary questions. May I begin?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not yet, Mr. Seselj. Shall we give the number for that transcript? Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P74, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Should it be under seal or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I would submit it should be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wonder why. That was -- the reason why it was tendered confidentially at the time was because the witness received the kind of protective measures at the time. But once it has been lifted, we can deal with it openly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: If the Chamber is satisfied on that, then that's satisfactory from my standpoint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Prosecution microphone off, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit it publicly. Yes, Mr. Seselj, do you have anything to re-examine?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have only two brief questions concerning, Mr. Drazilovic, your response to the last question asked by Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you recall that in March 2008, a decision by the Trial Chamber III was taken to lift the protective measures in your case?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you receive a document to that effect?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, since this was a confidential document, I'm not going to quote anything from it, with the exception of one single legal principle. Therefore, fear not. And I would kindly ask the Registry to hand over to Dr. Drazilovic a document dated 3rd of March, 2008, in Serbian. The original is in French. And also members of the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution can have a copy each. I'm only going to ask Mr. Drazilovic to look at page 3 and to read paragraph 1, and it doesn't contain any confidential information. It only deals with a legal rule applied by the Trial Chamber III. Can you please hand this paper to Mr. Drazilovic in the Serbian language. I hope that you have given copies in French or English to members of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see the point of putting this document, which is a court order, to the witness. You can put your question directly to the witness without having to show this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, I can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm going to read only the first paragraph on page 3 of this document, which reads: "Given that although the protective measures are always introduced in order to achieve an equilibrium between the protection of a witness and the rights of the accused, each witness may eventually decide for himself whether he or she will testify before the Trial Chamber without protective measures. Therefore, the pseudonym --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now I was able to read the passage, and I'm certain my colleagues will agree with me, but it's not for the witness to answer this question. It is for the Chamber. The witness is not a legal expert, and he is not in the position to deal with whether or not protective measures should be allowed or not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kwon, my intention was not to ask the witness about this. However, you are attacking me even before you heard what my question for the witness was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. What is your question, Mr. Seselj? Put your question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Drazilovic, do you recall this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you recall that this passage was contained in this document to the effect that each witness can eventually decide for himself whether to testify before the Trial Chamber without protective measures?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And at that time, the protective measures that had been applied to you were lifted?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: At that moment in time, was it clear to you, and if this was the position of the Trial Chamber, that I can use it and apply it in every other case of every other witness who wants to have protective measures lifted?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another document. I provided copies for the Trial Chamber and for the Prosecution as well, and I think that the witness can be shown this as well. These are delivery notes from the printing plant. Do I have to explain to you again why I am raising this or can I proceed with my question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Drazilovic, I would kindly ask you -- it's only two pages. These are photocopies of three delivery notes, three delivery notes; is that right? You are versed in publishing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Please do not mention the title of the book, because if you do so, there is a risk of us moving to a private session and for the transcript to be redacted. Therefore, do not ever mention the title of the book. Just give me a yes-or-no answer. Is this the book that is the subject of these proceedings? Just don't say the title of the book.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the title is correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The people from Registry who speak Serbian can verify this for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you see the number of the delivery note here?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you see the date? It says here "Zrenjanin" and what is the date?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Tell me the date.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 10th of September, 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you see the name of the printing plant in the heading?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it the Dragic Printing Plant from Zrenjanin?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Please take a look at the second delivery note and tell me the date.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 11th of September, 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the third one, the date?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 12th of September, 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How many books were delivered to the Serbian --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please pause between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters were not able to catch up to the speed the both of you are speaking. Please put a pause between the question and answer. I take it there should be an English translation of -- English version of this proces-verbal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no English translation, whatsoever, because, Mr. Kwon, the Registry did not allow me to proof the witness. They did not want to pay for the trip of my legal adviser and case manager. I'm calling 10 witnesses today without any preparation or proofing whatsoever. I received this by fax today. You can see the date, the 7th of June. I had no possibility to prepare my witnesses. I'm intentionally being put into the position of a wandering goose in the fog. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So what is your question in relation to this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Drazilovic, on the third day, on the 12th of September, how many books were delivered?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do we have proof here that protective measures in your case were lifted on the 3rd of March, 2008?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is to say, half a year had elapsed by then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Half a year later, the book was published containing the statements that you gave to me; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN DRAZILOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why, then, are they bringing charges against me because I published your statements six months after measures of confidentiality were lifted in your case? You see, Judges, what lack of seriousness there is on the part of Mr. MacFarlane in discharging his duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's not for the witness to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is now a question for the Trial Chamber. This is the very point of it. Now, this is me scoring a point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why did you not raise this in your examination-in-chief, how this issue arose in the context of the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is derived from Mr. MacFarlane's last question. And in response to that, the witness, himself, said that his statements given to my associates were published six months after his protective measures had been lifted. Find that in the transcript. The witness, himself, said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. MacFarlane, I didn't recognise you rose at the time. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you. With a view, hopefully, to being helpful to the Chamber, and for the record, the first document, which is the order that the accused made reference to, dated the 3rd of March, 2008, is already before the Chamber as Exhibit 31, just to assist on that point. And with respect to the broader question that the accused has raised of lifting and whether the protective measures were in existence, that will be the subject of submissions at the end of the trial and will involve a comparison of the extent to which the order rescinded or varied the original order. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. MacFarlane. Do you have anything further to ask the witness for your redirect examination, Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kwon, since the Prosecutor did not ask for his 65 ter document to be admitted into evidence, I am tendering the decision of the Trial Chamber of the 3rd of March, 2008, that contains the underlying legal principle that each and every witness can decide for himself whether he is going to testify under protective measures or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That is already in the evidence, so you don't need to tender it again. That's the --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When was this admitted? When was this admitted, Mr. Kwon? I don't remember that. Was that in that big package that the Prosecutor brought in on the first day of the trial?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think this was the part of the Prosecution's Bar Table motion, which we granted, and there is no issue. I don't think the Prosecution is challenging that at the time of this -- at the time of this delivery, the --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just in case, if, perchance, you had not admitted this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then have you concluded your re-examination, Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait and let me tender something else, and then I will be done. I tender these three delivery notes of the printing press to the Serb Radical Party that show that a total of 10.000 copies was printed of the book in question, and that these copies were being delivered over the course of three days in succession, and that this is irrefutable proof of the book being published in (redacted) 2008, which had not been contested earlier on, either. From the very beginning, we have all known that the book was published in (redacted) 2008.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have any observation, Mr. MacFarlane?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I hadn't seen the document. It's in Serbian, and not in English. It seems to me it's common ground the publication took place in (redacted) of 2008, so I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There is no challenge as to the date of the publication?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: No. It's set out in our pre-trial brief. I believe the phrase that we used was "early in (redacted), perhaps somewhere around the 1st of (redacted)," so that appears to be common ground.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this document supports the pre-trial --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given that we do not have the English translation of these delivery notes, we'll mark them for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit D4, MFI'd, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already told you that I have completed my cross-examination. I just wanted to tell you that I have officially asked the Registry to pay the travel expenses for my legal adviser, Dejan Mirovic, and Nemanja Sarovic, my case manager, so they could come a few days before the trial, come to The Hague, and help me prepare Defence witnesses and proof them. In prison, they set a particular office for those purposes. However, I never received an official answer from the Registry, why they did not accept that, although I spoke to quite a few representatives of the Registry. That is why I was not in a position to proof the witnesses, but you see how successful I am even without proofing and preparation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Drazilovic, that concludes your evidence. So on behalf of the Chamber, I thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask you something, Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: On an exceptional basis, yes, Mr. Drazilovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please allow me to exchange greetings with Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I kindly ask you to allow me that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is not for us - it is for the security people to decide - but I would say no. You can say something briefly now in open session. Otherwise, we are not in the position to allow you to approach the accused -- the witness -- the accused and say something. On an exceptional basis, we allow you to say something to the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing to say to him, actually. I have nothing to say to him. I would just like to shake hands with him, because I was hoping that I would be able to do that. After all, I haven't seen him in eight years, except on TV screens. It would really mean a great deal to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see any problem. Yes, please go on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I? Thank you. Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you. There is a small procedural issue that I'd like to raise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You may be excused. You may be excused. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I've just been -- I've just been advised that the issue that I wish to raise has been taken care of, so we don't need to deal with it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. MacFarlane, given that we admitted publicly the document -- the transcript, I'm wondering whether we can lift the confidentiality of the transcript that is related to the foundation part for the introduction of that document. I'm not sure -- I'm just raising, for the sake of consistency, the confidentiality of the portion of the testimony that was held in private session with respect to the previous witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: To change the status of the viva voce evidence to be consistent with the status of the document; is that -- is that the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We admitted the document publicly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, in my opinion, whether there's any reason to keep the confidentiality of those portions of transcript. The whole purpose of going into private session, according to you, was to introduce that document, which was allegedly confidential, but we admitted it publicly, so we'll lift the confidentiality of that portion of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I agree. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this transcript was never declared confidential by the Trial Chamber. This transcript was not confidential. After the meeting held in Belgrade, one copy was given to Zoran Drazilovic, and the other one was given to the lawyer, Petar Jojic. Immediately after that, we used this document as a public document and treated it as such. What it says at the bottom of the page: "Confidential, redacted," that was interjected later by the OTP, without any legal reason or grounds for it whatsoever. It was always a public document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No need to go back to that issue again. It's time for you to call your next witness, who is DS-2.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I call Witness DS-2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. While the witness is being brought in, can I remind you, Mr. Seselj, again, and as well as Mr. MacFarlane, the issue in this case is whether you violated the court order by publishing these witnesses' statement. It's not relevant, for the purpose of this case, whether what is stated in the statement was true or not or whether he was threatened. That has nothing to do with this case. Please bear that in mind when you examine the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't agree with that, Mr. Kwon, because at least mitigating circumstances in this case depend on the general circumstances under which certain statements were published. You have to allow for mitigating circumstances here as well. You cannot just forbid having them there altogether. It is a mitigating circumstance if a witness signed a statement that is a false statement, that was imposed on him, that is not the truth, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I will not repeat what I said, but I will see to it that the examination is limited to the relevant issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. If you could take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Following the decision made in another Chamber, you will be receiving the protective measures, which is: You will be called by a pseudonym, which is DS-2, and your face and voice cannot be heard outside the courtroom. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do, but I refuse to testify under protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: To cut it short, this Chamber has nothing to do with that order, because we cannot but follow the decision made in another case. So in order to lift the confidentiality, Mr. Seselj or Mr. Prosecutor should apply to that Chamber to that effect. So we have no say to that protective measures. Do you understand, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand, Your Honour. But as I've already said, all of this was topsy-turvy. It was a very long trip, too. It was very hard for me. I came as a witness for the defence of Mr. Seselj. Am I speaking too fast? Can you follow what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection, Mr. Kwon. I called all my witnesses as witnesses that would testify in public. Secondly, I now have an opportunity to refer to the position of Trial Chamber III; namely, that every witness can decide for himself whether he is going to testify before the Chamber without protective measures. This witness decided to testify without protective measures, and you don't have the right to impose such measures on him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I think and submit that the point that we're at right now and the issue is perhaps a small illustration of one of the big issues in this case, and that is Mr. Seselj's perception that, in some fashion, a witness makes decisions on whether the person is a protected witness, whether it can change in a variety of circumstances. The Jovic decision from the Appeals Chamber is very clear on that, that it's only lifted on order of the originating Chamber. So when the accused indicated he had a number of witnesses, I wondered whether he would be applying. And the evidence before you on the Bar Table motion indicates previous cases in which, in fact, Mr. Seselj did apply for variations or rescinding of protective measures, so he knows very clearly what has to be done, and I'm puzzled on why he didn't take steps and why he's asserting this position. But it arises from a fundamental understanding of who controls the process. The Chamber does, and for good reason, because that's the protection to a witness to ensure that they're not intimidating to attempt to retract or recant on the protective measures. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it by now, Mr. Seselj, you understand the Rules. As indicated by Mr. MacFarlane, until such time as the original Trial Chamber varies or rescinds the original protective measures, there's no way other than we just follow the existing protective measures. Let's not waste time anymore. It's now for you to examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kwon, I have to say this to you: I have no need to address Trial Chamber III to have protective measures lifted, because I have the position of Trial Chamber III, stating, ultimately, that each and every witness can decide himself whether he's going to testify before the Chamber without protective measures. All of my 10 Defence witnesses decided independently to testify without protective measures. You imposed protective measures on one of them yesterday, and I hope that you will not be able to impose protective measures on anyone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I said not to waste time. Start your examination, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I won't before a decision is made whether the witness is going to testify or not. He told you that he would not testify under protective measures. You cannot behave as if he had never presented any position whatsoever. The witness is not a mere object in this courtroom, he's not just a thing. He is a participant in these proceedings, just like all the rest of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Exactly. And like all the rest of us, we're subject to the Rules, Mr. Seselj. And the Rules are that this Chamber sitting at the moment does not have the power, of its own motion, to rescind the protective measures. I think you understand that very well. It's not a question of imposing protective measures on the witness; they're there. And there's a methodology by which they can be removed, but that process has not gone through. It seems to me it's a matter entirely for you now, whether you want to carry on with the protective measures being in place or whether you don't. That seems to be the choice you have.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to the decision of Trial Chamber III that decided on protective measures, the witness, himself, is entitled to lift his own protective measures. The witness is entitled to lift these measures himself. When I examined the first two witnesses, their point was that the statements given to me were public, and they agreed to have those statements published in my book. And now a witness appeared here again. I helped you yesterday with having the first witness waver and ultimately decide to testify under protective measures. Today, I'm not going to help you. If you are trying to get this witness to agree to testify with protective measures, then you go ahead and try to do that. I am not going to start my examination before the witness, himself, gives up on his own position that he will not testify under protective measures. He said that clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you are applying to this Chamber to lift the protective measures, we --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not asking you for anything, except to respect the will of this witness. This witness wants to testify in public, and he is resolute in his intention to testify in public only. The question here now is whether you are going to respect his decision and his will, which is based on the aforementioned decision of Trial Chamber III. So he does have legal grounds of insisting for -- for insisting on his own position. If the Trial Chamber said that ultimately each and every witness can decide for himself, then he, himself, decides. It is not for you to decide. It is for him to decide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We cannot disregard or ignore the existing protective measures. It is for you to decide whether or not to continue with your examination of this witness. You can withdraw this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not going to give up. I haven't even started my examination because you haven't created conditions for me to do that. When the witness introduced himself to you, signed the pseudonym sheet, he told you that he refused to testify under protective measures. This is still a pending problem. You haven't solved it. Once you solve this problem, I will start my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber -- in my opinion, the Chamber has made its position very clear. I would like you to start your examination, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How could I do that, because the witness said that he would not answer the questions under protective measures. How shall I start? Put a question to him and get silence from him, is that what you want?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Start your examination, Mr. Seselj. Ask your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Sir, do you still abide by your position, that you don't want to answer any questions until the protective measures are lifted?

utterances.speaker: DS-2
utterances.text: Yes, and I stand by that position. And may I address the Trial Chamber, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. MacFarlane, I think you wanted to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Again, more with a view to assisting than anything else, two points. The first is that you have before you, in Exhibit 33, a motion brought by the accused for a review of protective measures, so that the process is well known, well understood by the accused. And I think the Chamber's comments might reflect that point. The second point is: I don't know the identity of the witness yet, I don't know the witness's name, but I'm wondering if it would be appropriate, in closed session, to determine the name, because there was, if I recall correctly, one witness who was before Trial Chamber III who sought to have the protective measures rescinded, and Trial Chamber III didn't do that, so -- but I don't know if this is the witness. So I put that forward as a potential. If I'm wrong, then that route goes nowhere. If my recollection is correct, then that might be a reflection of Trial Chamber III's view of the matter. But I simply put that forward as a potential option here.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecutor switch off his mike, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber explained, both to the accused and to the witness, about the Rule. If both of them do not accept the Rules of the Tribunal, I don't think there's a point of keeping the witness anymore. Mr. Witness, are you still minded not to give evidence under the protective measures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may address you briefly. Do you allow this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber in the Vojislav Seselj case received a document confirming that I had never asked for any protective measures to be introduced, because I never asked for any, and I think that the Trial Chamber is fully aware of that. Therefore, I believe that this is sufficient grounds for me to testify in public, that nobody is threatening me or exposing me to any danger, and I would kindly ask the Trial Chamber to take into consideration my view that I am only willing to testify without protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I now understand your position, Mr. Witness. The point is this: You are called as a Defence witness, called by -- Defence witness, i.e., Mr. Seselj's witness. It is Mr. Seselj that wanted you to testify before the Tribunal. In order for you to testify in public, Mr. Seselj should have applied to the original Trial Chamber, i.e., Trial Chamber III, to rescind the protective measures given by the Chamber previously. Otherwise, we cannot hear you in public session. That's the Rule. So now it is for you to testify with the protective measures. Otherwise, we cannot proceed. Did I make myself understood to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. But as I said, unfortunately, I think that maybe we can reach a compromise, if I may say so, in the sense that Mr. Seselj might, in the meantime, apply for the lifting of the measures. And although I'm poorly and my health is not good, if that happens, I am willing to come back and testify again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or as a way of compromise you referred to, you can give testimony with protective measures, and after Mr. Seselj succeeded in getting that decision of rescission of protective measures, we can release or lift the confidentiality of all the transcript and video-tape later on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kwon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm asking the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understood what you said, but please understand my position as well. I experienced horrible things during my testimony. I was even threatened with the accusations of the contempt of court. So due to that, quite simply, I do not trust the Trial Chamber any longer, that they would do as you suggested and that they would take the decision as requested. Therefore, in other words, if I can only appear here as a witness and testify in public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to raise an objection, Mr. Kwon, that you, as the Presiding Judge, cannot create an agreement with the witness that imposes a certain obligation upon me. You want to reach an agreement with the witness that will force me to apply to Trial Chamber III to file a request for lifting the measures. I have here a crystal-clear position taken by Trial Chamber III to the effect that ultimately every witness may testify before the Trial Chamber without protective measures. I'm not going to risk that Trial Chamber III might change this. They may reconsider their principal position, and they may rescind it. And I published my book on the basis of this position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will not get into a legal debate as to the Rules. We made it clear as to the meaning of the Rule. So I will finally ask the witness and Mr. Seselj whether the witness and the accused are minded to proceed with evidence with protective measures. Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I refuse to testify with protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While we find it to be very unfortunate, the Chamber cannot find another way than allowing the witness to be excused. So, Mr. Witness, now you are free to go. Could you wait a minute until we draw the curtain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we need to have a break in order to proceed with the next witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: No, I was just rising --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll break for five minutes. --- Break taken at 4.42 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, is your next witness Mr. Jovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I call Mr. Nenad Jovic as my fourth witness. While we are waiting, is it possible for the Registry to tell me how much time I have used for the previous three -- or, rather, two witnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Twenty-nine minutes with Witness Drazilovic and fifty-six minutes with Witness DS-1.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am very economical with my time, and I can say that I'm even saving time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Jovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please make yourself comfortable. Please be seated. My understanding is that you are suffering from some back pain, so please don't hesitate to tell us if you need a break at any time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a problem with my centre of balance. It was bad yesterday, but today it is a little bit better, so I think I can cope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We appreciate it very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, you heard what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, after you have had your initial contacts with The Hague Tribunal, who was the first to mention the protective measures for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: I knew nothing about any protective measures. I was only asked to produce my passport to get a visa and that I would appear here as a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In the case against me?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the case against you. But I refused that, I didn't agree to do that. No, I won't do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So can I take it, then, that you were declared a protected witness against your will?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, totally against my will, because I know everybody, I can recognise their voices, I know what they did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If both of you put a pause between the question and answer, since you are speaking the same language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll do our best.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you recall who was it that mentioned your name for the first time in public as a protected witness in the case against me?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That was Natasa Kandic, and I have this CD here with me with a press conference that was actually a show broadcast on TV Fox on the 28th of November. And on the 7th December, I actually held this press conference, and I have a CD here which shows who it was who mentioned that for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did I schedule a preparatory interview with you before your appearance?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: For this appearance, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But this conversation never happened?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Because I couldn't bring my legal adviser or a case manager?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't explained to me why you couldn't do this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, is it possible for the Registry to take this CD, to make copies for the Prosecution, for myself, and possibly for the Trial Chamber in order for it to be admitted into evidence, because I have never seen this CD before. So the Registry may look into it and make a copy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have both the CD and the transcript, and I can give all that to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I had no contacts with Mr. Jovic prior to these proceedings, can we resolve this issue in this manner? I would like to continue my examination-in-chief while the Registry is making the copies of the CD and the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we put the transcript on the ELMO so that the Amicus, as well as the Chamber, can take a look. Is it in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's not in B/C/S. It is in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something else, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also took two newspapers that came out on the 8th of December, after the conference that was held on the 7th of December. So all of Serbia knew what I had said, how I was mistreated and all the things that were done to me, also that I said that I didn't want to be a Prosecution witness. It was Mr. Antonetti who called me as a Chamber witness, and that is how I testified via videolink.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope this is not considered to be my time. I would not discuss this with Mr. Jovic, that is to say, what the Prosecution did with him beforehand, so that we do not go too far from the topic of these proceedings. I agree with what you said, that I should focus only on disclosing the identity of protected witnesses, not anything else, so I think it would be better if somebody from the Registry made copies of the material we have just received, rather than people looking at the version on the ELMO and trying to find their way. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll deal with this issue of admitting this CD, as well as the transcript, at the end of this session. In the meantime, let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You mentioned that Natasa Kandic - that is the last thing you said in response to my question - was the first person who spoke on Fox TV in November 2007 and presented your name and surname as a protected witness in my trial?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I said, quite precisely. You will see what Nenad Jovic from Mali Zvornik will tell you when he comes in to court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: As a protected witness?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was that on the 28th or the 29th of November?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: It's possible that it was the 29th. I'm not very good with dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who is Natasa Kandic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I asked that question several times. Last time, Judge Antonetti -- well, if she's an employee of the Court, she should be punished, and if she's not, then the punishment should be double.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We have to wait for the interpreters a bit.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of The Hague Tribunal initiating proceedings against The Hague Tribunal because she disclosed your name as a protected witness in these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: I never heard of that. I proposed that to the Court because I do not have the financial capability to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Before Natasa Kandic said that, did anyone know that you were planned to be a Prosecution witness in these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: No one knew. I didn't know either. They made me an offer. I refused, and I left these papers unsigned. I left. I said, I don't need -- I mean, I don't want to repeat all of this. We're wasting time. I said, I don't need protective measures. If necessary, I'm going to face the Court and testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And when you heard that Natasa Kandic mentions your name publicly, your name as a protected witness in the proceedings against me, what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Then I told all my friends about this. I told them my code-name, my pseudonym, VS-83, I think. That's what I read. And I told everybody about that, and I said that that was a futile thing for me. And I did not expecting anything. I went to Republika Srpska and never had any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Where did you hold this press conference after Natasa Kandic's TV show?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: In the Serb Radical Party. I would have organised it elsewhere if it was somebody else's leader that was concerned. However, since it was about you, then I addressed the Serb Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, when you heard Natasa Kandic mention your name as a protected witness in the proceedings against me, then you addressed the Serb Radical Party and you asked that they organise a press conference for you. Right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I called and I asked to speak to some lawyer, and a man answered the phone and told me that I should come there and that we would reach an agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you give any interviews to the press?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, to "Pravda." We have "Pravda" here. There were several newspaper houses present there, if I can put it that way, "Novosti," "Kurir," "Blic," all of these dailies published that, and people from Sweden even said they saw me on TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can you give these newspapers to the representatives of the Registry so that they can provide copies of this interview with you for all of us?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: That's why I brought all of this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, are you going to order someone from the Registry to do that for us, to make copies of these newspapers so that we can see this? This is a bit unusual, but also it is not the usual thing to bring witnesses in without any kind of proofing. Had Mr. Jovic given this to me, I would have made copies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something? On every newspaper, it says "Page 20." That means that it's there. Then on this other one, it says, in pen, "Page 5," so that's the page you should look for so that you don't have to go through the whole newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, can you show us the longest interviews from these newspapers for the cameras, the longest interview that was published?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: It was "Pravda." Let me just find it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Please turn it to the Trial Chamber, and then I assume that the cameras are going to pick it up?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Here's what it says: "I'm not going to lie against Mr. Seselj." I'm showing it to the Trial Chamber now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What was the date of that "Pravda"?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: The 8th, in the morning. I'll have a look now. It should be the 8th of December, because the press conference was on the 7th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the year is ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: 2007. So was that eight or nine days after Natasa Kandic appeared on television?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Can I put this down now?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, you can put it down. Thank you. After these interviews for the newspapers - I see that the Trial Chamber is not reacting to my proposal, that the Registry take this over - did you take part in some kind of public panel discussions?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I did, before and after that. I'm a supporter of the Serb Radical Party ever since the inception of the Serb Chetnik Movement. I used to be a member, too, but we all know why I was excluded, because of disobedience, because I stayed in Tenja without the group. But, yes, I did take part in all the public panel discussions that were organised on every anniversary of your stay here in The Hague in detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you speak at these public gatherings?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the trade union's hall. It was a scholarly gathering called "Stop to the Tyranny of The Hague." I spoke in public. I told people about what happened to me with these investigators, everything that happened to me later in October last year. I was even on video-beam, because there were a lot of speakers, and then I explained all of this on video-beam too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember when the annual assembly of the Committee for the Defence of Vojislav Seselj was held in Zemun?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. I became a member then, and I'm a member of that committee.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you say that you became a member, does that mean that you signed a paper joining the committee for my defence?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we are speaking so fast once again. In Zemun, I signed a paper in order to become a member of the Committee for Defending Vojislav Seselj, and I became a member of this association, and I took part in their work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Does this association function as a kind of non-governmental organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
