utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear your answer because both of you spoke so fast, overlapping. But before that: Mr. MacFarlane, do you object to dealing with this "Pravda" newspaper at the end of the session, after having taken a look?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I would like to take a look, but, fundamentally, I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would appreciate that the Court Deputy could make a photocopy of it and hand it over to the Amicus Prosecutor. Could you repeat the last question? I will read it for you: "Does this association function as a kind of non-governmental organisation?" What was your answer to that question, Mr. Jovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, my answer was, Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know? However, if you do know, don't say the title of the book out loud. Do you know why these contempt proceedings are underway, because of which book of mine? Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know -- you don't know the title of the book?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that some of the texts in this book that are part of the charges are your statements given to my associates?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm pleased, because I gave these statements with that intention, allowing you to use all my statements in the electronic media, in a court of law, anywhere. Heaven forbid that you be in this position again. So the media, internet, court, everywhere. You can use all the statements that I gave. I signed them, and also they were stamped in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let us be very specific on part of your very exhaustive answer. Does that mean that you gave your consent that I publish your statements in my book?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely. You didn't have to ask me anymore. I gave my consent.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have completed the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, did you say something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I said that I have a problem with my veins. It's going to be hard for me to turn this way and look at you, so please don't understand this by me refusing to look at you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it would be a good thing if Mr. MacFarlane was to be relocated somewhere else within this courtroom. He is too close to witnesses, anyway, and perhaps that was done on purpose. You see, witnesses are half a kilometre away from me, and Mr. MacFarlane is only half a metre away or so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Physically, I cannot handle this. I cannot look this way and that way and then this way and then that way again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Witness, nobody's going to take it as any form of rudeness, that you don't look at the person who is asking you questions. Indeed, because we are the people who have to determine what you say, it might be better that you simply look at us anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I'd like to start off, sir, by asking you to take a look at a document that's been tendered in these proceedings and marked as an exhibit as 55Q. And I'm not sure where the Court Usher is at the moment. Perhaps -- we have a 55Q in both English and in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we put the English on the ELMO and give the Serbian version --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: To the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- to the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- after having shown it to the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, me too, I think. I should be receiving a copy as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: That has already been provided to the accused in the usual way and was included in the Bar Table motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's unfortunate that e-court is not working today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you to read the entire statement, but, rather, if you could read the first two paragraphs. And I have some questions once you're done that.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: From up here, you mean [indicates]? Oh, down here. Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While we're waiting, can the Registry tell me how many minutes I used in the direct examination of Mr. Jovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, you can ask it during the break.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I wouldn't want to do it during the break because I have to be checking on Mr. MacFarlane to prevent him from using more time than I have used. That is important for me. If I used up only 10 minutes, then he is allowed to use only 10 minutes as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is for the Chamber to decide how long the other side should cross-examine the witness, not for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovic, my question is a relatively narrow one, and that is: Does the information set out in this statement, in terms of your -- it purports to be your name and village and other personal information. Does that name you, and is it accurate?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: But the date of birth --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: What is the date of birth?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: 2nd of October, 1957.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. In the statement here, there is no date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, there isn't. I don't even know when this was given at all and to who. SUP, Mali Zvornik. "Issued by SUP, Mali Zvornik." What is this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't follow your objection, Mr. Seselj. It is the witness who has raised the issue of date of birth, not the Prosecution. You can ask it -- clarify it during your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Is the information contained in that paragraph, which names you, purports to, and village, and ID card number and so on, is that accurate and does it identify you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is what I'm telling you, sir. It's not correct. First of all, there is no Municipal Court in Mali Zvornik. I live in Mali Zvornik. I live three kilometres away from the centre, two and a half kilometres. We don't even have a misdemeanor judge, let alone a court of law. What do you mean a court in Mali Zvornik, a municipal court in Mali Zvornik? I mean, really, this is something I don't know about at all. We're going to see what the rest says, but this is not correct. It is in Loznica that there is a municipal court. That is 20 kilometres further down the Drina River. We don't have a municipal court. We never had one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Let's move to the next paragraph, aside from the Municipal Court, the paragraph that names you -- purports to name you, and the village where you live, and so on. That's the paragraph I would like you to focus on, and my question is: Is that accurate, and does it identify you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but there is no ID card number. It says: "Issued by Mali Zvornik SUP." My ID card was issued in Belgrade, and I can show you. We received them from Belgrade. They are being taken to Belgrade to be certified. And it says here: "Place of issue: Belgrade." And there's a stamp as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I take a look at Mr. Jovic's ID card?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I'm concerned, you may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not now. Let's proceed, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Sir, after that paragraph there is a heading called "Statement," and then it starts out: "I have given several court-certified statements ...," and so on. Can you take a look at that paragraph and advise whether or not you provided that statement?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you. And let's just be really clear on the preceding paragraph. It starts out: "I, Nenad Jovic, of Radalj village, Mali Zvornik ..." Does that name you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question? I had some problems with --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: In the short paragraph which sets out your name, I suggest, I just wanted to confirm that that portion that says: "I, Nenad Jovic, of Radalj village, Mali Zvornik ..." My question is: Does that mean you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but my ID card number should be here. Can we look on the back side to see who certified this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, maybe we don't have the same document. In my copy, we have the number of the ID. It's 3109 [as interpreted]. Now I'm perplexed. Why is he saying that there is no ID number? Do we have a different document in front of us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Mr. Seselj, I found it. Yes: "I, Nenad Jovic, of Radalj village, Mali Zvornik municipality, ID card number 31091, issued by the Mali Zvornik SUP, hereby give voluntarily the following court-certified statement." So shall I keep on reading? What was your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: My question is: Does that identify you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course it's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, you've described in direct examination that you wish to testify in open court and that you didn't have any particular concerns, but I'd like to take you back to earlier years, because my suggestion to you is that you've gone through a transformation of sorts for reasons that aren't clear, and so I'd like to start at the beginning. And I suggest to you that you have actually given several statements to the Office of the Prosecutor, starting in the year 2003, perhaps as many as five or six statements; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct, but it is also correct that -- I explained this at the previous trial, I went through all this. All of this was based on blackmail, all of this was fabricated. Is there anyone else on this world to whom I should say that Rita Pradhan kept me sitting in a chair for 14 hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Well, let's just take a look at that for the moment. I suggest to you that you gave a statement to the OTP in July of 2003, and then had a further meeting and gave a statement in September of 2003, and then returned, gave a further statement in October of 2005, and then returned and gave a further statement in late October of 2006, and then returned and gave a statement in June of 2007, and then returned and gave a statement in July of 2007, and then returned and gave a further statement in October of 2007. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. There are quite a few correct things. But since a third country was guaranteed to me, a better life, money, hotel accommodation here in Holland, the company of beautiful girls whose services I can make use of at the expense of the Tribunal, I just wanted to see what they were going to do with me, because my life was at stake. But once I learned that all these were lies, because whatever they say is a lie, and you will see this here, and after that I held this press conference and I gave a statement to Dr. Vojislav Seselj's Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Well, let's go in order here, because it's obvious, and you've just agreed, that you kept going back to the OTP and were co-operating with them and providing statements. So I'd like to go through in a bit of detail and direct your attention to one of the first statements, perhaps the first, on the 10th and 11th of July, 2003. And I suggest to you that you gave a detailed 23-page statement, and included in that statement is this statement: that you were willing to testify, but that you're concerned about yourself and the safety of your family. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: I remember then an APB bulletin was issued for me when I was in Montenegro. Rita Pradhan said that I had to come forward immediately. So under this pressure of an APB and a potential indictment, I eventually ran away. I fled the apartment where I was sleeping. I went over there and said, I don't want to sign anything, and I left. Rita told me that the policemen guarding the building would be instructed to arrest me and take me to a jail, and then, You are going to be taken to The Hague and that you are going to sing like a canary. I thought of my kid at the time. And people who wanted to harm me probably lost something -- everything in the war; their house, their family, whatever. I don't know who it was that she sent after me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like to ask you a question. You've been referring to and refreshing your memory on the basis of Exhibit 55Q. I'd like you to recall on the basis of your own recollection. And perhaps the Court Usher could retrieve the exhibit at this point, because I would like to be very clear on your relationship with the Office of the Prosecutor, in terms of the statements. In connection with the first statement that I referred to, 2003, for one thing, I would like you to advise on the accuracy of this: It's my understanding that you voluntarily approached the Belgrade Field Office and wanted to talk to the investigators in 2003. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I remember, but I didn't do that of my own free will. I received a summons, and I'm sorry that I didn't keep it. Actually, I was hiding the whole affair because I didn't want to be accused of co-operating with The Hague Tribunal. That's what I said last time when I appeared at a trial. But no problem, we can do that another three times, if necessary, because that is the truth. If you wake me in the middle of the night, I will tell you the truth. As for lies, I have to learn them by heart and then I stutter when I utter them. I have been having medical problems since 2003 because of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: There is no doubt in your mind that during the course of that 2003 interview and statement, that you indicated that you were willing to testify, but that you were concerned about safety; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody asked me to testify until the second or the third encounter, when they came up with this thick statement already prepared in advance. And they wanted me to sign this against Mr. Seselj, and they told me that I was going to testify against Simatovic and others afterwards. I hadn't seen Mr. Seselj for a long time. What can I tell them about him? Listen, I was a policeman, and I have no idea what the strategy of the party was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: My question was not with respect to testifying against Mr. Seselj, in particular, but my question was whether or not there is a discussion about testifying and that you said that you were concerned about safety. That's my question, and I'd like you to answer that.

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to answer your question. This was presented to me as a kind of interview, that there would be no court proceedings to follow. They asked me if I knew something, given the fact that I was in the war, and then, of course, if I didn't know anything, it was no problem. However, later on all of them gathered together, and then they kept me for 14 or 15 hours, and they threatened me with prison. That was their strategy of destroying a whole family. I had a small child at the time, and they were hiding in a forest in order to save their lives, because their lives were threatened because of me. Who could save me from that? I'm not raising my voice to you. The two of us are just conversing. I'm telling you the truth. I am telling you how it was, and that's what I did the last time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: And from what you said, the truth is you were concerned about safety for you and your family?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Listen, I didn't want to talk to them about anything. If anyone suspected that I was co-operating with The Hague Tribunal, they would kill my family. Therefore, leave me alone. But they told me, If you try to go home, the policeman -- the guard at the gate would take you to prison. That was blackmail, and all these promises about third countries, and money, and other promises. I have a friend, and I talk to him on the phone sometimes. So who's the liar here, the investigator, or is it me?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Well, I think you've, in part, just answered that question, because you indicated that if it was known that you were co-operating, you may be killed, and yet for several years you were co-operating and providing statements. Isn't that accurate?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: I was only interrogated, but I did not co-operate. There was a statement written against this man here, Mr. Seselj, and I was only required to sign it and I would have been paid for it. And they told me, Look at you. You walk in such old war shoes, you have no money. You just need to sign this. And I didn't want any money, and I don't want any money from you either. I have a child that was bullied in school. Other kids kicked him because I was known to have been in the office of The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you for your advice on that. Let's move forward a bit to subsequent events. I'd like to get your comments. And I would direct your attention, in particular, to an interview on the 25th of October, 2005, where you discussed the fact that you are a radio amateur and have a licensed radio station in your home, and that you communicate with people from all over the former Yugoslavia. Do you recall that event and that discussion?

utterances.speaker: NENAD JOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember, but I'm telling you I have a license, and I've been a Ham Radio operator for 20 years. I have a license issued by the Ministry for Telecommunications. It's my hobby, and I talk on the radio with the people in Slovenia, in Mostar. We are on friendly terms.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kwon, I expected you to ask Mr. MacFarlane to explain the relevance of these questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: The relevance will emerge very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not necessary. Mr. Seselj, you interrupted the interpretation of what the witness was saying, so we couldn't hear. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said -- may I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We heard until that it was your hobby and you talk on the radio with people in Slovenia and Mostar: "We are on friendly terms." And what did you say after those words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. He asked me the reason for that, and I said, I may have even talked to you. I probably conducted about two million conversations. I talk to people in Canada, to everyone. Maybe that's why he's asking me. That's the point of my being a Ham Radio operator. If you ask me this kind of question, what else can I answer? This was not a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. MacFarlane, I see the clock. For the planning purposes, can I know how much more do you have for the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I would expect roughly 10 to 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then we'll take a break now. We'll break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. MacFarlane, I was informed by the VWS that the witness was not feeling well and didn't want to continue with the remainder of his evidence. So the Chamber allowed the witness to retreat, and we'll continue with the remainder of your cross-examination tomorrow, first thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So in the meantime, we proceed with the next witness, who is Mr. Rankic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before that, Mr. Kwon, I have a procedural objection that I must express. In the case against Slobodan Milosevic, who represented himself, the Trial Chamber gave the Prosecution 60 per cent of the time, compared to the time used by Mr. Milosevic. In the trial of Mr. Radovan Karadzic, the Trial Chamber has allocated much more time to Mr. Radovan Karadzic for cross-examination than it did to the Prosecution. In the proceedings against me, you are using an apothecary balance. Mr. Kwon, you just don't have any patience with me. Why don't you have any patience with me? We worked perfectly well yesterday without you, and I want to just state an objection. May I do so?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, you are free to raise any objection at any time. It is not for you to determine how much the Prosecution is allowed to cross-examine the witness. We'll take into account what you submitted. Let's --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not up to me to decide; it is up to you. But it is up to me to raise an objection if I observe injustice. I cross-examined -- I examined Mr. Jovic 16 minutes. Cross-examination by Mr. MacFarlane lasted already for 27 minutes, and he indicated that he would need another 15 minutes. I would just like to know which criterion you are applying when making these decisions, because this should be based on the equality of arms of the parties in the proceedings. You may decide that Mr. MacFarlane can have 100 hours, but this will create an impression in the public that you are biased and that you are arbitrarily taking decisions. You are answering to my objections spitefully. You are spiteful in your responses. I am not expecting anything good to come from you. I am not expecting any justice to be -- or fairness to be granted to me. But I would like the whole world to know how you conduct yourself as a judge, and I think everybody is clear on that by this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber has made clear its position. Let's not waste time anymore. Let's bring in the next witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does that mean I'm not going to call any witnesses anymore?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it not Mr. Rankic that is your next witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait until I call the witness, Mr. Kwon. Are you going to call my witnesses or am I going to do that? Yes, Mr. Rankic is my next witness, but I supposed that it was up to me to call him and that he would be ushered into the courtroom. If you're going to take my role in this courtroom, let's switch places. I think that I will be more successful in the place that you are taking, and you, Mr. Kwon, would be much worse and your performance would be much worse than mine if you took my place. Am I going to call Mr. Rankic or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, you didn't allow me to call Mr. Rankic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You submitted your submission in relation to the order of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The practice applied in this Tribunal is that parties call their respective witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Rankic. If you could take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please make yourself comfortable. Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Rankic, have you already testified as a court witness in the main trial against me here?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the 11th and 12th of May last year, I testified here viva voce.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you provide several statements to my associates, wishing to be a witness for my defence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you inform my associates that all your statements that you have provided to us could be made public?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that in a book of mine, I published your statements given to my legal associates and others?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you give your consent for these statements of yours to be published in my book?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was this consent explicit in response to their question as to whether you agree that this be published in such and such a book? Did you agree to that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Rankic, did you appear at some public gatherings where my books were promoted?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes. If necessary, I can tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How many such events were held?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Two or three.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you attend any scholarly gatherings, some of which were international ones, where the violation of my procedural rights in The Hague proceedings was discussed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It's not only that I was present, but I also addressed the present via videolink. There were several thousand people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you give your full name and surname on the occasion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I gave my full name and surname throughout. Had that not been the case, I would have filed charges against whoever would have said that I was VS-017.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you ask The Hague OTP to provide protective measures to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When was it that you first found out that these protective measures were imposed on you nevertheless?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: When I was brought, by way of a deception, here to The Hague for the first time in 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you explain at these gatherings, at these events, how you were treated by the Hague OTP?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what did you say about that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I said that pressure was first brought to bear against me in 2003, that the investigator, Paolo Pastore-Stocchi, in the presence of Sabine Schulz, another investigator, exerted pressure against me, to provide a statement as he liked, not as I had wanted to. Dissatisfied with my statement, in the presence of Ms. Schulz and Ms. Marina Krstic, an interpreter, he tore up my first statement, saying that they have witnesses who claim that my statement does not correspond to their statements or, rather, the facts as they had happened, and that he also had something against me, as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did they threaten you with criminal proceedings against you in The Hague because you were an official of the Serb Radical Party and a member of its Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did. In the beginning of August 2003, I was threatened by Mr. Stocchi, and in the beginning of January 2004, the investigator Rita Pradhan. I think that's her name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Please do not actually say the name of the book that this is all about. Just say yes or no. Do you know what the title is of this book where I published your statements?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember that this book was promoted at an event in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know where this promotion event was held?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I am sorry, I really do not remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was it at the trade union's hall?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you attend?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions. I insist that Mr. MacFarlane gets the amount of time that corresponds to the total of the time that I had used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to provide a brief submission or commentary on the last point made by the accused. It's clear that he has shifted his strategy in the trial. He recognises that it's very easy and very quick to demonstrate current consent. My intention is to show the evolution or transformation of a witness, which requires more time. That is the strategy. And for the purposes of truth-seeking, I'm asking for the Court to exercise some discretion so that I can show that transformation of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seselj did raise, actually, the case of Dr. Karadzic. It's a matter of public record that the time spent upon cross-examination allowable to Dr. Karadzic is often far greater than the time spent on examination-in-chief by the Prosecution. So it seems to me to be a matter which is well known in this Tribunal, that sometimes it takes longer to cross-examine than it does to examine in chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to object first yet again. Mr. Morrison, you are not allowing me to object?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, this time we're not hearing you. Mr. MacFarlane, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You want me to walk out, Mr. Kwon? Order the guard to lead me out. What do you need me in this courtroom for? How can Mr. Morrison say that Mr. Karadzic has a lot more time than the Prosecutor does, and then he compares that to our situation, in which he puts me in the role of the Prosecutor who is conducting the examination-in-chief, and Mr. MacFarlane is being put in the position of someone who is defending himself. There is a difference between a professional and a self-represented accused. A self-represented accused always has the privilege of conducting longer direct examination and longer cross-examinations. Mr. Kwon knows that full well, because he was a Judge in the trial of Slobodan Milosevic and he is now presiding over the Chamber that is trying Mr. Karadzic. And now other rules apply to me. I have to have a privilege, as a self-represented accused, to have more time for direct examination and cross-examination than the representative of the Prosecution here. Do not -- do not confuse me with the Prosecutor here. That is what I had to say to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is the Chamber that monitors the fair and expeditious conduct of the trial. As long as the parties remain in the relevant issues, the Chamber would allow it to continue. The Chamber will monitor the --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Mr. Kwon, this morning -- or, rather, today, when you were saying, at the very outset, that we should stick to relevant issues, you were referring to both Mr. MacFarlane and myself. You actually meant me, and now, all of your criteria have gone completely down, as far as Mr. MacFarlane is concerned. However, this is not the first time that you are showing how partial you are as a Judge. You are well known for being that way throughout, Mr. Kwon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's a misrepresentation of what I said. That relevance issue -- test equally applies to both the Prosecution as well as the Defence. Yes, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Sir, you've outlined your current views and current thinking on the publication of your name and your statement by the accused. I'd like to take you back to earlier years, and I'd like to ask you to comment on what appears to have been an evolution or a transformation over the years. I'd like to take you back to August of 2003, when you were interviewed by investigators with the OTP, the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: And, in fact, you have been interviewed on quite a number of occasions. On my count, at least five times. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Four or five times, possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: So you kept going back to the Office of the Prosecutor, to sit down with the investigators and talk to them about your knowledge, and, in most of those instances, to provide a statement to them; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: No, that's not the way it was. For the most part, they were pressuring me to make a statement. Otherwise, they would send the Serbian police to bring me in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Let's move to the statement that you provided on the 6th of September -- pardon me, 19th of September of 2006. So this is some three years later. And you were interviewed by a Prosecutor and several investigators, and provided a statement. And in that statement, you made this statement: "I am willing to testify before the Tribunal about the events I described ..." And then this is the important part. "... but I have significant concerns for my safety, and I would only testify if I can be guaranteed that my safety would not be compromised." Do you recall talking to the investigators about safety, and do you recall insisting that that be included in that statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: No, that is absolutely incorrect. They said to me that I was in danger in Serbia, allegedly, from the Serb Radical Party, and possibly some foreign elements too. Therefore, they said that it was desirable, from that point of view, that they give me these protective measures. When I testified viva voce here, I denied all of this that the Prosecution presented, because they wrote this up in a way that suited them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: You agree, though, that there was a discussion about the issue of safety and that the investigators provided you information concerning your own safety; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was discussed, but I did not insist on protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Let's move forward from September of 2006 to a couple of months later in November of 2006, where you, once again, sat down with the investigators and provided a statement. And in that statement is the following: "I'm willing to testify before the ICTY about the events I described, but I have significant concerns for my safety, and I would only testify if I could be guaranteed that my safety would not be compromised." And there was a Serbian version which you signed. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course I recall that. However, at the time I was in house detention here in The Hague, where I spent all of two months, and my movement was restricted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Once again, in the year 2006, in June, in particular, do you recall meeting with the investigator and your telling the investigator that you have been approached by a group of people in Belgrade and told not to play with your life, and that your son had answered a phone call where the caller threatened to blow the witness up? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that. However, the threat was not addressed to me directly; rather, to my son. However, I'm not sure that this has anything to do with this case. Perhaps this was totally apart from all this that has been going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: That's your current thinking, but I'd like to take you back to that time which is what we're talking about is your thinking at an earlier stage. And I suggest to you that you were certain at that stage, or strongly believed, that the incidents took place because of your co-operation with the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: No, no, that is not correct. I was never sure that it was that way. The Prosecution referred to that as a conversation between them and myself, but I'm not sure that it was a real threat at all. It is possible that the Prosecution fabricated the threat altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Once again, I'm taking you back to that point in time in 2006. And I suggest to you that you were concerned at that time that these events took place because of your co-operation with the OTP.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: No, that has nothing to do with the OTP. Of course, my fear was the natural fear of a parent for a child. That is only natural.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: So you agree that there was a concern that you had at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Of course, for the safety of my own child. I was afraid on that account.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: And I suggest to you that there is a discussion about the prospects of a temporary relocation and whether that would be sufficient. And perhaps other protective measures were discussed as well, but a temporary relocation to another country was discussed. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: First of all, I have to point something out. One of the reasons why I was brought to The Hague was, allegedly, that they had lost all of my statements or, rather, that they had all been stolen at Belgrade Airport, and that, therefore, I had to come to The Hague to provide all of these statements again. In fact, that purported to be the main reason for bringing me to The Hague. Once I arrived in The Hague, the trial of Mr. Seselj had started in the meantime, and they took advantage of my presence here in The Hague to call me as a witness. Of course, I did not accept that. And since they had deceitfully brought me to The Hague, I escaped from The Hague in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Well, you were anticipating my next question, because I wanted to ask you a question in relation to the disappearance of the statement or documents during the flight. On the 17th of September, 2006, I understand that you met with a Prosecutor and investigators, that that information was provided to you that some material had gone missing, and that you did not express any concerns for your safety with respect to that. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: No, of course not. As for myself, personally, I never felt any fear of anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I'm speaking now of the disappearance of the materials. You advised the investigators that you weren't particularly concerned because of that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Of course, why would I be concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll take that as a yes. I suggest as well that on the 18th of September, 2007 - that's a year later - that you were met by a number of people, and that you advised that you would not attend an interview with the OTP, and that you didn't want to testify for either party in the Seselj trial, and that you didn't have any security concerns at that stage. Do you recall advising people that you didn't want to testify for either party?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: No, that's not the way it was. If the Court allows me to do so, I'll explain what had actually happened. This is how it was: The Office of the War Crimes Prosecutor called me to come to the Special War Crimes Court. Mr. Mrdak called me, asking me to come to Ustanicka Street in Belgrade, the War Crimes Court there, in order to talk to Mrs. Dahl. However, I didn't want to talk to anybody. If I were summoned by the Court here in The Hague, I would come and say, viva voce, what it was that was troubling me and what had actually happened. So this is what I did last year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Do you recall having discussions with -- do you recall having discussions with respect to relocation to a third-party country, and initially discussions about the prospects of going to Sweden?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was mentioned, but I had no other way of getting my documents except by accepting to co-operate with the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: The reason that you had discussed the prospects of Sweden was that you had someone that you knew there, and that was an appealing third-party -- third country for you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: But instead, the plan ended up being a relocation to the Netherlands; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: No, that was never mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: But that did take place? You were relocated to the Netherlands for a period of time; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I said a moment ago that I did not move to the Netherlands. Rather, I was brought to the Netherlands by deceit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: You were provided with accommodation, allowances, and an identity card; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't have any documents on me, except for this little card that was with a code. As for accommodation and money, yes, I was staying at some apartment. I received 25 Euro a day for food expenses. And you, yourself, should know what 25 Euro a day means in the Netherlands.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: You were also provided with a mobile phone and contact details of protection personnel who you could contact 24 hours a day; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: And there were no restrictions on your movements within the Netherlands, you could go wherever you wanted to; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, automatically, by virtue of the fact that I didn't have a passport with me, my freedom of movement was restricted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Movement within the Netherlands, itself, was unrestricted, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was or whether it wasn't. I didn't experiment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Sir, I want to show you two documents that have been tendered in these proceedings. For the record and for the Chamber, they are marked as 55D and 55E. And, sir, I would like you to take a look at the beginning few paragraphs of both of these documents, and I'll have a few questions for you in connection with the first few paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like you to take a look at, first of all, 55D. Perhaps the Usher could help you in focusing initially on 55D. I'd like you to look at the first paragraph, in particular. It provides information that purports to include your name and some personal information. Can you read that over and advise if that, in fact, identifies you and provides information of a personal nature concerning yourself?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Well, I hope I don't have to read all of this. I'm simply checking whether this is my statement, the one that was certified in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I'm asking you to take a look at the very beginning of the statement. It names -- purports to name you and provide information concerning you. And my question is: Is that accurate? Does it identify you and is it accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Let's move, then, to Exhibit 55E, the second one, and my question is the same thing. Take a look at the opening paragraphs, and does that identify you and provide personal information concerning you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: As far as I know and as far as I am familiar with the Rules of the Tribunal, I have the right to request protective measures. It is up to the Court to decide whether these measures would be granted or not. However, no one has the right to impose protective measures on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: One last question. Let's try this from a different angle. Do you know the date upon which the protective measures that the Court ordered concerning you were lifted?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Fine. No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. MacFarlane. Do you like to re-examine Mr. Rankic, Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my estimate, my examination-in-chief lasted between five and seven minutes. Mr. MacFarlane's cross-examination lasted almost half an hour. Am I entitled now to 25 minutes for redirect?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As long as your re-examination is limited to the things that arose from the cross-examination by Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the cross-examination was absolutely irrelevant. Mr. MacFarlane dealt with the matters that have no relation whatsoever to the bill of indictment. The bill of indictment was based on my publication of witness statements. However, what Mr. MacFarlane dealt with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you minded to put questions to the witness or not?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kwon, due to your tendentious and unfair conduct throughout the whole day today, I refuse to put any additional questions to this witness. I would like to thank this witness for appearing as a Defence witness. And I really cannot tolerate any longer your unfair conduct. My tolerance is limited as well. Perhaps tomorrow, if I'm in a different mood, things will be different, but today I cannot stand you anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, at any stage during your involvement with the Tribunal, was there ever any actual physical threat to you made, in terms of somebody attempting to physically harm you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: If we are talking about a classic maltreatment and threats, no, those didn't exist. However, whenever I was summoned, either directly or through my family, it was always accompanied with a pressure to the effect that if I fail to respond, they would send police to bring me in. In my view, this is a form of threat. And as I said, in classical terms, nobody maltreated me or threatened me in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: So to put it simply, in your view, the threats were psychological, as opposed to physical?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rankic. That concludes your evidence. I'd like to thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I have the right to additional questions, in view of the question put by Mr. Morrison, and I think I'm entitled to put questions even after the Bench have put their questions. Is that correct, Mr. Morrison? You're a good lawyer. You understand that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before putting the question, let us know the question, what it is about. Tell the Chamber first what your question is about.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My additional question concerns the question put by Mr. Morrison, but I'm not going to tell you in advance what I'm going to ask him. But it is based exclusively on what Mr. Morrison asked the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, the plain Rule is if there is a judicial intervention which raises something, then both parties are entitled, as a matter of courtesy, to explore it. You can, and Mr. MacFarlane can, should he wish to, but you go first.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not mind that at all, Mr. Morrison. I'm counting on the correctness of you, Mr. Morrison, and that of Mr. Hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: One question. Mr. Rankic, when Judge Morrison asked you about the nature of threats you received, can you tell us precisely, according to your understanding, where these threats came from?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN RANKIC
utterances.text: Exclusively from the Prosecutor's Office.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That was my question, and I intentionally did not want to tell Mr. Kwon what the nature of my question was going to be because nobody can force me to divulge in advance what I am going to ask. And, of course, I have no objection to Mr. MacFarlane putting one question himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: I doubt whether you wish to, Mr. MacFarlane, but this is your opportunity, should you wish to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: No, I see no point in asking questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rankic. I thank you again for you coming to give your evidence to the Tribunal. Now you're free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kwon, since we only have 10 minutes left, I suggest that I call my next witness tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's only 10 or 12 minutes, and I wouldn't like to interrupt my examination-in-chief. And in addition to that, I am quite frustrated and unable, therefore, to commence my examination-in-chief. I need some rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your point has been taken. We'll resume tomorrow. What time is it scheduled? 2.30. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Tomorrow, we'll begin with Mr. Jovic, and then we continue to hear the other witnesses. 2.30 tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: If I might rise on one issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: The Chamber will recall that I was midstream in the cross-examination of Mr. Jovic, and then he didn't return. He wasn't given the customary warning not to have communication with anyone because he is still testifying. I'm just wondering if there's some way that that advice could be communicated to him so that he understands his obligations to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it that VWS can convey that order from the Chamber to the witness. The hearing is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 8th day of June, 2011, at 2.30 p.m.

--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.49 p.m.,
